To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service, Towson — Aria 3 service and eight trial days back

Last month I told Dana I would report back on Harbor Point once my writer had been through a real trial. My Stenvale Aria 3 has now survived eight days of a civil trial since coming home, so here is the promised review.

I dropped it off Monday, October 19, and picked it up Tuesday, October 27: six business days against the ten quoted. Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road in Towson, with free parking in back. Having somewhere local to take the machine, rather than shipping it away, was part of the appeal.

The original estimate was $285 for recalibration, number bar inspection, cleaning and a firmware update. The completed work included a full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number bar depression sensor, internal cleaning and an update from firmware 4.0.7 to 4.2.1. Gloria also found that the internal battery was holding about 60 percent of its rated capacity. She asked before replacing it, quoted $25 for parts and labor, and waited for my approval.

The final bill was $310, paid by card at pickup. I paid personally, as I do for all my equipment; there was no reimbursement from the court. I think that was fair for the work done, and being asked about the battery before it became a charge matters to me. The invoice gives a 90-day warranty on the work.

The important part is how it writes. My first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. After eight trial days, I am comfortable saying the repair has held up under actual working conditions, not just a few minutes of testing at home.

The machine also came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never had that from anyone before. It is a useful record to keep with the machine, and I appreciated it.

A Stenvale Aria 2 loaner was provided, so I was not left without a writer. It did have a problem: the tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I reported that to Gloria by email. When she notified me that my machine was ready, she said they would repair the arm. I cannot say whether that repair has since been done.

The phone arrangements are the real weakness. Their stated phone hours are Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4 only. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress. It rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up for me to leave a message. Gloria emailed the next day about the battery, but that does not make the phone coverage adequate. For anyone working a Monday docket, those hours are particularly inconvenient. I would not count on being able to reach someone promptly by phone.

Dana, based on this visit, I would trust Gloria with my Aria again. The work was good, the turnaround beat the estimate, and the final price was reasonable. I would go in knowing that telephone access is limited and would check the loaner’s adjustments before leaving. Those are real reservations, but they do not undo the good work on my own machine.

Maureen
